scope: Mathematical vector interpretation and test-only byte identity; no admission, signing, origin status or general fold engine.

numeric.probabilities: Exact rational arithmetic. Fractions use rational strings or numerator/denominator integer strings. Explicit finite dyadic constants such as 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 in fixed tables denote those exact rationals; do not infer measured probabilities from agreement.
numeric.integerCertificates: Integer coefficients, counts and finite certificate identities are exact. State counts and partition witnesses retain their handed finite domains.

logarithms.meaning: Entropy, phase and information values computed with Math.log2 are explicit binary64 approximations, not exact real certificates.
logarithms.exception: A vector or reused historical sample may declare its own decimal precision or tolerance; the specific test must state it.

jsonIdentity.objectKeys: Sort object keys lexicographically recursively before JSON serialization.
jsonIdentity.arrays: Preserve every array's order, including constraint witnesses, coefficient order, effective act order and timestamps. Never sort arrays merely to make hashes equal.
jsonIdentity.numbers: Use the handed finite JSON numbers with standard JSON encoding; no decimal rounding, epsilon normalization or replacement of approximation by an exact claim.
jsonIdentity.hash: SHA-256 of the resulting UTF-8 JSON bytes, demonstrated only in tests. A hash establishes byte identity under the declared projection, not theorem truth.

claimCollectionProjection.domain: Fixed distinct static claims with explicit unique IDs, fixed values and origins, and no order-sensitive widening, withdrawal, epoch or mark interpretation.
claimCollectionProjection.operation: Keep every claim field and sort this explicitly named collection by its unique ID before canonical JSON encoding. This sorting is a projection specific to that unordered collection; it does not reorder the object or its effective acts.
claimCollectionProjection.duplicates: Duplicate IDs fall outside the distinct-claim domain and are refused; conflicting duplicates are never resolved by first/last arrival or a chosen value.
claimCollectionProjection.limit: Equal hashes across arrival permutations apply only to this fixed unordered projection. Distinct effective mark order, including equal-time widening/signature sequence, remains visible and may have different values and hashes.

research: Claimed general hypotheses, C3 unqualified odd-period argmin and any unspecified objective stay open. Passing finite vectors alone does not establish unrestricted proofs or independent origins.
